correctness.rationale: For all integer t>=2,m>=3, every blade K_(m+1) survives deletion of any two edges. Cut-vertex series resistance gives the exact weighted within-blade Kirchhoff objective with hub-pair multiplicity 1+(t-1)m. Woodbury inversion on the complete-blade Laplacian gives the single-damage and three positive same-blade incident-interaction expressions; disjoint or interblade edges add. All edge-pair types are exhausted by spoke/rim, blade membership, and incidence. Eight exact rational differences and the positive-denominator sign analysis give strict six-level rankings without unverified integer ties. A standalone program checks all symbolic difference identities and 57 independently grounded full-graph rational inversions; no finite experiment is used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The identified contribution is the six-level all-parameter optimization hierarchy, its second-worst transition at blade width three, and the exact same-blade-only interaction criterion. Existing inspected work uses Kirchhoff-index outage vulnerability (Koç et al., 2013), gives unperturbed windmill resistance indices (Sardar and Xu, 2024, accessible abstract only), or computes edge-defect resolvents for a single complete graph with removed edges (Tamura, 2026). The last yields usable local formulas but does not state the weighted bouquet objective, interblade cancellation, or the interdiction ranking. Similar accessible published records concern different invariants or graph families. Full-text nonaccess and possible implicit formulas are residual risks.
residual_risks: The Sardar–Xu windmill full text was not available; it may contain extensions beyond its abstract.
Further unindexed two-edge windmill vulnerability comparisons may exist.

value.rationale: The two-link interdiction objective is a natural electrical robustness metric with a 2013 archival network-vulnerability motivation. The result gives a complete all-pairs six-level risk ordering for an infinite two-parameter family, exact maximizer and second-place counts, a genuine m=3 versus m>=4 second-best transition, and the counterintuitive zero synergy of two failures sharing the hub but belonging to distinct blocks. It addresses placement of two failures, not arbitrary ad hoc parameter computation; limitations and lack of an application-level power-grid model are stated.
